extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), applicants, assignees, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards governing who may represent a U.S. patent applicant or owner, how powers of attorney are appointed/revoked, Customer Number practice, and correspondence address/signature requirements in U.S. patent applications and related proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee power of attorney revokes prior powers
rubrics_metrics.description: A power of attorney by the assignee of the entire interest revokes all powers given by the applicant and prior assignees if the assignee establishes their right to take action as provided in pre‑AIA 37 CFR 3.73(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 324. Ordinarily, the applicant will still have access to the application (MPEP § 106). A power executed by an assignee who establishes rights under pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.47(a) may revoke a power given by inventors who signed the declaration (available inventors) per pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.32(b)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Form PTO/SB/80 and statement under pre‑AIA 37 CFR 3.73(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/SB/80 may be used by an assignee of the entire interest to revoke a power of attorney and appoint a new power of attorney; the assignee signs the power of attorney and either the assignee or newly appointed practitioner must sign a statement under pre‑AIA 37 CFR 3.73(b) for the application in which the general power of attorney is to be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 324, subsection V. for who can sign the Statement Under pre‑AIA 37 CFR 3.73(b) (Form PTO/SB/96 or equivalent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers of attorney during interference or derivation proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: While an application is involved in an interference or derivation proceeding, any power of attorney or revocation thereof should be forwarded to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition under 37 CFR 11.9
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual not registered under § 11.6 may be given limited recognition by the OED Director to prosecute a specified patent application(s) upon showing circumstances that make it necessary or justifiable and that the individual is of good moral character and reputation; limited recognition does not extend beyond the specified application(s) and is not granted to those who have passed the registration exam or whose registration application is pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special provisions for individuals ineligible due to immigration status: limited recognition may be granted consistent with authorized employment/training period and subject to immigration rules; recognition automatically terminates if the individual ceases lawful U.S. residence, authorized employment/training, or the immigration status; not granted to non‑U.S. citizens residing outside the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation in international applications (37 CFR 1.455)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants of international (PCT) applications may be represented by attorneys/agents registered to practice before the USPTO or by an applicant appointed as a common representative; where no representative is appointed and multiple applicants exist, the first named applicant entitled to file in the U.S. Receiving Office is considered the common representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointment of an attorney/agent, or common representative (PCT Rule 4.8) must be effected in the Request, Demand, or in a separate power of attorney submitted to the Receiving Office or International Bureau. Powers of attorney and revocations should be submitted to the U.S. Receiving Office until issuance of the international search report. See MPEP § 1807 for additional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment/revocation by less than all applicants or owners requires petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers giving or revoking a power of attorney generally require signature by all applicants or owners. Papers signed by less than all applicants/owners will not be accepted unless accompanied by a petition under 37 CFR 1.36(a) (for revocation) or 37 CFR 1.183 (for appointment) and the required fee showing sufficient cause or extraordinary situation where justice requires waiver of 37 CFR 1.32(b)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions should be directed to the Office of Petitions. The appointment/revocation is not accepted until the petition under 1.36(a) or 1.183 is granted; a newly appointed attorney/agent may not submit documents (e.g., IDS) into the application until petition grant. Acceptance of such papers may result in more than one attorney/agent prosecuting the application, requiring all such parties to sign subsequent replies. See In re Goldstein, 16 USPQ2d 1963.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature and reply requirements when multiple responsible parties exist
rubrics_metrics.description: When more than one person is responsible for prosecuting the application, replies must be signed by the appropriate combination of practitioners and applicants. Examples: (A) If coinventor A has given a POA to a practitioner and coinventor B has not, replies must be signed by the practitioner for A and by coinventor B. (B) If coinventors A and B have each appointed their own practitioner, replies must be signed by both practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When acceptance of papers results in multiple practitioners/applicants prosecuting the application, each must sign all subsequent replies and must indicate whom he or she represents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence held with attorney/agent of record (37 CFR 1.33)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an attorney or agent has been duly appointed to prosecute an application, correspondence will be held with the attorney or agent unless some other correspondence address has been given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An attorney/agent who assigns a correspondence address different from where mail is normally received must still keep client information confidential (37 CFR 11.106) and remains responsible for responding to Office notices (37 CFR 11.101, 11.103, 11.804). The Office will generally not undertake double correspondence with an applicant and their attorney/agent; see MPEP §§ 403.01(a), 403.01(b), 403.02, and 714.01(d). If double correspondence is attempted, include form paragraph 4.01 in the next Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 4.01 (Double Correspondence) and examiner handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 4.01 notifies applicant that double correspondence with applicant and applicant's attorney/agent will not be undertaken and that applicant must conduct future correspondence through the attorney/agent of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner notes: (1) On first direct reply from applicant include paragraph and send a copy of action to applicant. (2) Do not send copies of subsequent Office actions to applicant if additional replies filed. (3) Status letters from applicant may be acknowledged in isolated instances. See MPEP § 403.01(a) for additional info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer Number uses and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: A Customer Number may be used to (A) designate the correspondence address of an application or patent (address associated with the Customer Number becomes the correspondence address), (B) designate the fee address for maintenance fee correspondence, and (C) submit a list of practitioners such that those practitioners associated with the Customer Number would have power of attorney (37 CFR 1.32(a)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Customer Number can be used to designate correspondence address, fee address, and to establish POA for practitioners associated with that number; the correspondence address Customer Number provides full access to the USPTO patent electronic filing system (PatentCenter). See MPEP § 1730 and § 502.05 for electronic filing details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of practitioners by referencing Customer Number
rubrics_metrics.description: The association of a list of practitioners with a Customer Number permits an applicant to appoint all practitioners associated with the Customer Number merely by reference to that Customer Number (i.e., without listing practitioners individually).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding/deleting practitioners via PTO/SB/124 updates the list of persons authorized to represent applicants who appointed all practitioners associated with that Customer Number, avoiding the need to file additional papers in each affected application. Appointment by Customer Number is optional; applicants may continue to name practitioners individually (subject to the <10 named practitioners rule in 37 CFR 1.32(c)(3)). If an applicant appoints both a Customer Number and an individually named list, the action will be treated as appointment of the practitioners associated with the Customer Number only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer Number cannot appoint a law firm; must appoint specified practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: The Customer Number practice does not equate to appointment of a law firm; the Office prohibits appointment of a law firm because it cannot verify whether a particular practitioner submitting a paper is associated with the specified firm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office permits appointment of all practitioners associated with a specified Customer Number because it can ascertain practitioner association from Customer Number records. A law firm should promptly remove any practitioner who leaves the firm from the list associated with the Customer Number to prevent that practitioner's access to applications; departing practitioners must obtain a new power of attorney to continue representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent practitioner restriction with Customer Number
rubrics_metrics.description: Design patent practitioners registered under 37 CFR 11.6(d) can only practice in design patent matters; a power of attorney naming practitioners associated with a Customer Number may include only practitioners authorized to practice in the applicable patent matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a Customer Number associates a design patent practitioner, that Customer Number can only be used to establish POA in design patent matters, even if practitioners authorized in all patent matters are also associated with the same Customer Number. See MPEP § 1502.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer Number administration and Mail Stop EBC
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO accepts requests and changes to Customer Number information through the patent electronic filing system; Mail Stop EBC is the Office mail stop for Customer Number correspondence (requests for Customer Number, data changes, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested forms: PTO/SB/125 (Request for Customer Number), PTO/SB/124 (Request for Customer Number Data Change), PTO/AIA/122 or PTO/SB/122 (Change of Correspondence Address, Application), PTO/AIA/123 or PTO/SB/123 (Change of Correspondence Address, Patent). Electronic upload instructions available via the Customer Number Upload Spreadsheet at www.uspto.gov/Ebc. Persons authorized to change Customer Number info: (1) a registered practitioner associated with the Customer Number, and (2) the person who requested the Customer Number (signed Form PTO/SB/125).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on multiple Customer Numbers and correspondence addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will not recognize more than one correspondence address (37 CFR 1.33(a)); applicants are strongly cautioned not to appoint more than one Customer Number for a particular purpose (e.g., correspondence address) in a single communication, as such action will not have a cumulative effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inconsistencies exist between an address resulting from a Customer Number and any other correspondence address provided, the Office will generally resolve in favor of the Customer Number address or the application data sheet (37 CFR 1.76(d)). Applicants may use different Customer Numbers for different roles (e.g., one for correspondence address and another for POA), but only the Customer Number associated with the correspondence address will allow access to the application in PatentCenter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of filing without a correspondence address
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application accorded a filing date is not complete and no correspondence address is provided, the Office cannot notify the applicant to complete the application and pay the surcharge; the applicant is considered to have constructive notice as of the filing date and will have 2 months from the filing date to complete the application before abandonment occurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periods for completing the application may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136. See MPEP § 601.01 et seq. for requirements for a complete application. The correspondence address may be different from the applicant's post office address (e.g., the applicant's registered attorney).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.33(a) requirements for applications filed on/after Sept 16, 2012
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing an application, a correspondence address must be set forth in either an application data sheet (§ 1.76) or elsewhere in a clearly identifiable manner in any paper submitted with the application filing. A daytime telephone number should be supplied in a clearly identifiable manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will direct all notices, official letters, and other communications relating to the application to the person associated with the correspondence address. For electronic submissions, an electronic acknowledgment receipt will be sent to the submitter. The Office generally will not engage in double correspondence with applicant and practitioner; if more than one correspondence address is specified, the Office will select one and may select the address associated with a Customer Number over a typed address. The correspondence address may be changed by parties set forth in paragraph (b) (patent practitioner of record or the applicant), and prior to appointment of a power of attorney under § 1.32(b) it may also be changed by any patent practitioner named in the application transmittal papers acting under § 1.34.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements for amendments and papers (37 CFR 1.33(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments and other papers filed in the application (except certain written assertions under § 1.27) must be signed by: (1) a patent practitioner of record; (2) a patent practitioner not of record who acts in a representative capacity under § 1.34; or (3) the applicant (§ 1.42).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless otherwise specified, all papers submitted on behalf of a juristic entity must be signed by a patent practitioner (37 CFR 1.31). Where papers from a prior application are used in a continuing application and the correspondence address was changed during prosecution of the prior application, an ADS or separate paper identifying the correspondence address to be used for the continuing application must be submitted or the Office may not recognize the change (37 CFR 1.33(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination and supplemental examination correspondence/signature rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All notices and communications for the patent owner(s) in reexamination or supplemental examination will be directed to the correspondence address in the patent file. Amendments and other papers in such proceedings on behalf of the patent owner must be signed by the patent owner (or all owners if more than one) or by an attorney/agent of record, or by a registered attorney/agent not of record acting in a representative capacity under § 1.34.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double correspondence with the patent owner(s) and the owner’s attorney/agent, or with more than one attorney/agent, will not be undertaken. See § 1.33(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hierarchy for selecting correspondence address when multiple provided (pre‑AIA rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: When more than one correspondence address is specified in filing papers, the Office will select one address according to the following order: (A) application data sheet (ADS); (B) application transmittal; (C) oath or declaration (unless power of attorney is more current); and (D) power of attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more than one correspondence address is specified in a single document, the Office will select the address associated with a Customer Number over a typed correspondence address.
